title: myrsine lehmannii
intro: Myrsine lehmannii, commonly known as the 'Guayabilla' or 'Puka', is a plant species native to the tropical regions of the Americas. It is a type of flowering plant in the Myrsinaceae family, valued for its medicinal properties and health benefits. The leaves of Myrsine lehmannii have been traditionally used to treat various health conditions, including fever, rheumatism, and skin disorders, due to its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. The plant's bioactive constituents, including flavonoids, alkaloids, and phenolic acids, contribute to its therapeutic actions, which include antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial effects.
